newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira surges through 980 vs mark on EMU optimism.
newsitem.headline: Lira surges through 980 vs mark on EMU optimism.

text.p: The lira surged through the 980 lire barrier against the mark on Tuesday on a wave of EMU optimism and a surge of stop loss orders linked to options, dealers said.
The lira had not reached this level against the mark since February 13 and dealers said the Bank of Italy may be tempted to step in and buy the German currency.

"Already yesterday we saw buy orders for marks from Italian banks which made us suspect that they were acting on behalf of the Bank of Italy, " said a dealer in London. "At the moment we are just making deductions."
"It's reasonable to think that the Bank of Italy will be vigilant. Excessive oscillations are disliked whether upwards or downwards," said an Italian dealer.
"Up until now we have not seen any intervention but if the cross should move towards 975 the Bank of Italy would intervene," the dealer added.
Some dealers said that buying was linked to options in the 975 area which, if reached, could push the cross rate further towards 970 lire to the mark.
But others see no further room for the lira to appreciate and expect profit-taking to take the Italian currency down to 980/982 to the mark.
At 0953 GMT the lira was trading at 978.60/8.90 against the mark after a morning high of 975.75.
